reasoning: L'Oréal — defensive growth compounder, 10.5% position at €348.
LVMH — luxury franchise recovering off Asia trough, 9.7% position.
SAP — European tech leader with cloud ARR momentum, 14.2% position.
Airbus — aerospace duopolist with decade-long backlog, 8.7% position.
TotalEnergies — dividend yield 5%+, integrated energy hedge, 11.5% position.
Danone — staples ballast, dividend aristocrat, 13.5% position.
Schneider Electric at €269.50 — quality industrial, FCF +28% YoY, sub-30 P/E, electrification secular; 8-share sleeve ~€2,156 fits inside the 15% position cap and the PEA basket.
Quality-at-a-discount add on SAP's -4.7% software-sector rotation day; fundamentals intact, entry near support.
Danone averaging-down at €63.28 (-6.6% from entry) — staples dividend aristocrat, fundamentals intact, PEA-eligible. 8 shares ~€506 stays inside cash budget and keeps Danone under 15% sleeve cap.

LVMH tagged my pre-drawn €485 trim line (closed €487.65). Sell 1 of 2 shares to lock the gain at fair value and lift cash above my non-negotiable €100 gate — keeps a half-position for continued compounding.

SAP at €140.26 (-9.9% from my €155.77 blend) sitting on support after a software-sector rotation; cloud backlog and FCF intact, P/E reasonable, PEA-eligible. Four shares ~€561 fits my cash and lowers my cost basis on a quality name I already conviction-hold — average down, not chase.

Pre-arm my -15% stop on SAP at €129.11 (151.89 blend ×0.85). It's my worst open position at ~-10% and the only one without an armed stop; the watcher enforces my hard risk limit if the rotation turns into a real break, freeing capital above my €100 gate.

Sanofi at €76.36 — the healthcare gap in my book, filled with quality at a fair price: P/E ~12, strong FCF, debt/equity well under 1.0, dividend growth over two decades, PEA-eligible. 18 shares ~€1,374 is 14% of the book, inside my 15% cap, and leaves €681 dry.

Cap discipline, not a thesis change: Schneider is 21.6% of a €9,909 book against my hard 15% limit, and it has been over since the 17 April entry (€2,156 on €10,000 was never 15%). Selling 3 takes it to 5 shares / 13.5%. Electrification thesis and FCF intact — the sleeve was simply mis-sized from day one.

Danone at 19.8% of book breaches the same 15% cap, a drift created by my 11 May average-down at €63.28. Selling 7 at ~€70 leaves 21 shares / 14.8%, keeps the staples ballast and the dividend, and books a small gain on the added tranche rather than letting one defensive name run a fifth of the fund.

Air Liquide at 170.32, sitting on the floor of its 25-day range and -6.6% off the high on 0.8-1.2x average volume while cyclicals rip — the defensive sleeve being sold to fund the melt-up, not a fundamental break. Industrial gases on 15-year take-or-pay contracts, four decades of uninterrupted dividend growth, debt/equity ~0.5, P/E ~24 inside my 30 cap, PEA-eligible, and materials is a sector I own nothing in. 6 shares ~1,022 is 10.2% of book, a starter with room to add lower rather than a full-size bet.

Legrand at 138.80 is -10.9% off its high with a volume-confirmed floor rather than a falling knife: capitulation at 128.70 on 1.87x volume, a 9% recovery on declining volume, now quiet at 0.54x. Passes the whole checklist — ~20 years of uninterrupted dividend growth, debt/equity ~0.6, strong FCF conversion, P/E ~20 against Schneider's ~30 for the same electrification end-demand, PEA-eligible. 5 shares (~EUR 694, 6.9% of book) is a starter that leaves EUR 254 to add lower.

Cap discipline plus liquidity, in one order. Schneider is 15.09% of a €10,129 book against my hard 15% limit — a breach created by a +13.5% run from €269.50, not by a purchase — and selling 1 share takes it to 12.1% while raising cash from a dangerously thin €254.51 to ~€559. I own Legrand for the same electrification demand at a P/E of ~20 versus SU's ~30, so this trims the expensive expression of a thesis I keep, and it is sized to 1 so my remaining 4 shares still exactly cover the armed 284 and 229.08 rails.

Ratchet the Airbus gain floor from €201 to €205. The base has walked up — the last low of consequence is €206.30 on 3 August and every close since is €210 or better — so €201 sits under the 31 July low, which is history now. €205 books +18.2% on my €173.46 entry, keeps three shares on a confirmed delivery cycle, and deliberately stops short of the €210.90 seven-session low: a floor tucked under one week of consolidation is a whipsaw, not a rail. Same correction I made at SU €284→€294.

Execute by hand the rail that the sweep did not execute. €199 was drawn below the €202-206 shelf precisely so it would fire on a genuine retracement of the August advance; that retracement happened — €197.24 on 1.31M shares, the heaviest volume of the window, then €196.18 — and the order sat there through both. Books +13.1% on 2 of 3 from €173.46 and leaves one share of a confirmed delivery cycle, deliberately unrailed, because a one-of-one stop on a €196 stub is the SAP error wearing a new suit.

Hand-execute the €288 gain floor the sweep skipped for the second close running. €288.20 then €286.75 is a genuine break of the entire August base, not the 1% chop that had me move this line down from €294 in the first place; books +6.4% on 2 of 4 from €269.50 and leaves 2 shares exactly covered by the armed €229.08 rail.

Re-draw the Schneider gain floor from €294 to €288, below the €291.80 close of 24 August and the whole August base. The €294 line was breached on the close twice in six sessions without firing while the name went nowhere — a floor buried inside the chop churns €590 of a compounding position for a 1% wiggle. €288 books +6.9% on 2 of 4 shares and fires on a genuine break rather than on noise; the 2-share €229.08 disaster rail still covers the other half, so all four shares stay accounted for.

Re-draw the LVMH exit from €412.59 to €424.00, just under today's €425.35 low. The old level was pure arithmetic (€485.40 entry × 0.85) drawn in July when the price was €453 — the mandate maximum, not a level on the chart. Today broke the €443 double bottom of 4 May and 20 August on 727k shares, the heaviest in the window, with RMS, KER and EL confirming at their own 60-day lows; that is a de-rating with no floor beneath it, and continuing to risk another 4.3% of the position to prove a point the sector has already made is not patience. Sized 1 of 1 because a stub cannot be partialed — the partial-rail doctrine that fixed the SAP error has no application to a single share, and pretending otherwise is how a broken stub survives forever.

Open the financials sleeve I have never owned, at market, because the diagnosis is worth participating in and not merely observing. Munich Re passes the whole checklist — P/E ~11 against my 30 cap, no dividend cut since 1969, fortress Solvency II, German and PEA-eligible — and it is the one sector where the rate impulse driving my entire book lower is a tailwind instead of a headwind. 1 share (~EUR 503, 5.2% of a EUR 9,751 book) is a starter with room to add lower, not a full bet. Deliberately unrailed: a one-of-one stop on a single share is the SAP error wearing a new suit.

Ladder a second Legrand rung at €134.00, the middle of the €133.20–137.35 shelf it held 24–27 August, above my standing €128.70 capitulation bid. Schneider is now fully exited at €286–288, so electrification is expressed only here at 7.1% of book while I hold a quarter of the fund in cash — the cheap twin deserves the size the expensive one had. Deliberately NOT at €140.90: buying the day after a +4.4% pop on the window's heaviest volume is chasing by my own definition. At fire, 8 shares is ~11.4% of book; with the €128.70 bid behind it, 11 shares is ~14.4%, inside my 15% cap.

Close the Airbus stub at market, +12.3% on the €173.46 entry. I already took 4 of 5 shares at €204.80 and €196.18 and left this one deliberately unrailed — correctly, because a one-of-one stop cannot be partialed. But that reasoning forbade a stop, not a decision. The August advance is fully retraced from €217.05 to €194.80, and the last two sessions are the window's two heaviest prints (1.26M, 1.15M) into its lowest close at €194.42. A €195 stub I have promised never to rail, in a name rolling over on rising volume, earns nothing and funds nothing. Frees a slot and €194 for the sleeve that is actually working.

Second Munich Re share at market €512.80 — 1.9% above my own entry three sessions ago, which is not chasing by any definition I have used (chasing was Legrand at €140.90 the day after a +4.4% pop on the heaviest volume of its window). The 8 September gap out of the €510–528 shelf has been fully closed in five consecutive higher closes on rising volume (392k yesterday against 277k and 308k before it); the shelf it held all July and August is reclaimed. P/E ~11, no dividend cut since 1969, fortress Solvency II, German and PEA-eligible, and it is the one name in my book where the rate impulse grinding OR/BN/SAN/AI lower is a tailwind. 2 shares is €1,026, 10.5% of a €9,757 book, inside my 15% cap. Remaining committed bids of €873 clear €1,691 of cash in any firing order with €818 spare.

Open a starter at market ~EUR 102.32 in the one factor that is beating me, rather than a fifth coat of the trade I already own the losing side of. BNP is the laggard inside that factor: it fell from EUR 112.80 on 10 August to a EUR 99.93 intraday on 27 August on 3.46M shares, the heaviest print of the window, and has since built an eight-session shelf between EUR 100.22 and EUR 104.80 on volume falling back to 1.3-1.7M. P/E ~7, a rising dividend, French and PEA-eligible, and I am buying the cheap twin while Allianz and Generali sit at highs, which is the same reason I own Legrand and not Schneider. I will name the exception rather than hide it: my D/E < 1.0 screen is meaningless for a bank, so the balance-sheet test here is CET1 in the low teens and the same fortress-capital argument I used for Munich Re's Solvency II. 4 shares is EUR 409, 4.2% of a EUR 9,759 book, with room to add lower, and it leaves EUR 1,280 against EUR 873 of committed bids.

Double the BNP starter at market ~EUR 102.32, the same price I paid yesterday, because 4.19% of book was a timid size for the one factor that is beating me and an unchanged price one session later is not chasing by any definition I have used. The shelf between EUR 100.22 and EUR 104.80 built on the 27 August capitulation at EUR 99.93 is intact, P/E ~7, rising dividend, French and PEA-eligible, CET1 in the low teens standing in for the D/E screen a bank makes meaningless. 7 shares is EUR 716, 7.3% of a EUR 9,757 book, well inside my 15% cap, and it leaves EUR 972 against EUR 712 of committed bids.

Pre-draw the add I said I had room for when I opened this starter at €170.32: €164 is the middle of the €160–171 shelf Air Liquide spent April through June building, not a level invented from today's chart. Eight down closes on volume shrinking from 732k to 470k is the defensive sleeve being sold to fund the industrial melt-up — take-or-pay contracts, four decades of dividend growth, D/E ~0.5 and a P/E inside my 30 cap have not moved. Sized to one share (~€165 with fees) so it and my standing €128.70 Legrand bid for 3 (~€387) both clear €559 of cash even if they fire the same day.

Cut the leg that is still standing. L'Oreal at EUR 383.80 is the only long-duration name in the book at the top of its range rather than the bottom (EUR 384.65 high on 7 September), so it is the only duration I can sell without selling a low — BN is six cents above an armed floor, SAN and AI are already fully spoken for by rails. I closed LVMH on 4 September on the view that this complex is re-rating with no floor and then kept the twin; this is the other half of that decision. Sized 1 of 3 and not 2 of 3 on purpose: two shares leave a railable pair, one share leaves the unrailable stub the Airbus lesson says never to create. Books +10.2% on the 17 April entry, takes the sleeve to 7.9% of book and the OR/BN/SAN/AI duration cluster from 50.5% to 46.5%.
